questions.question: Which of the following best describes the primary pathophysiological mechanism responsible for the peripheral edema observed in severe protein-calorie malnutrition characterized as Kwashiorkor?
options: Marked hypoalbuminemia leading to decreased intravascular plasma oncotic pressure and subsequent fluid shift into the interstitial space.
Severe hypernatremia causing acute intra-arterial volume overload and localized renal fluid retention.
Excessive secretion of aldosterone secondary to adrenal hyperplasia, driving systemic isotonic fluid retention.
Impaired renal excretion of inorganic phosphate leading to secondary hyperparathyroidism and widespread tissue swelling.

questions.question: Leptin, an adipokine critical for long-term energy balance, regulates appetite and metabolic rate by acting on specific neuronal populations in the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus. How does leptin modulate these pathways?
options: It inhibits pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons and activates agouti-related peptide (AgRP) neurons.
It activates pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons and inhibits agouti-related peptide (AgRP) neurons.
It activates both POMC and AgRP neurons simultaneously to maintain metabolic homeostasis.
It inhibits neuropeptide Y (NPY) neurons while suppressing POMC synthesis in the paraventricular nucleus.

questions.question: The endogenous synthesis of niacin (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide precursor) from the essential amino acid L-tryptophan requires enzyme pathways dependent on which combination of micronutrient cofactors?
options: Thiamine diphosphate (Vitamin B1), Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C), and Calcium
Pantothenic acid (Vitamin B5), Biotin (Vitamin B7), and Selenium
Pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (Vitamin B6), Flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD), and Iron
Tetrahydrofolate (Vitamin B9), Cobalamin (Vitamin B12), and Zinc

questions.question: In contrast to osteoporosis, osteomalacia is specifically characterized by which histomorphometric bone tissue alteration?
options: A proportional loss of both organic bone matrix and bone mineral content, maintaining normal matrix mineralization.
Excessive, localized osteoclast-mediated bone resorption resulting in cortical thinning without osteoid accumulation.
Uncontrolled trabecular hypermineralization caused by abnormal chondrocyte proliferation at epiphyses.
An accumulation of unmineralized collagenous osteoid matrix due to defective mineralization.

questions.question: Which intracellular multiprotein kinase complex functions as the primary nutrient sensor for essential amino acids—particularly intracellular leucine concentrations—to upregulate muscle protein synthesis via translation initiation?
options: Adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK)
Nuclear factor kappa B (NF-kB)
Mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1)
Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPAR-alpha)
